recipes.name: Breaded SPAM Steaks
ingredients_raw: 1 (12 ounce) can fully cooked luncheon meat (such as SPAM®), cut into 1/4 inch slices

steps.text: Heat oil in a deep-fryer or large saucepan to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Gently press the luncheon meat slices into the flour to coat and shake off the excess flour. Dip into the beaten egg, then press into bread crumbs. Gently toss between your hands so any bread crumbs that haven't stuck can fall away. Place the breaded luncheon meat slices onto a plate while breading the rest; do not stack.
Deep fry the luncheon meat a few slices at a time until hot and golden brown, 3 to 5 minutes. Drain on a paper towel lined plate before serving.

raw_recipe.description: Luncheon meat is breaded and fried in this quick and easy dish.

review.reviewBody: grew up [n hawiaii like anything spam

This was a really neat way to make SPAM. I didn't use this recipe as a "snack style" recipe. I used this in mind for a dinner, using the Lite version of SPAM, served with Uncle Ben's Brown Rice and Quinoa with Red Bell Peppers and Steamed Broccoli with a Italian cheese sauce. Was just what I was aiming for. In the process of dredging, out of habit, I doubled dipped the SPAM, coating the slices with the Italian bread crumbs. And it really put a nice crust on the finished product. Also didn't deep fry but yet panned fried with just enough oil to cover as it was cooking. Was delish and will totally make again.

This is almost exactly the recipe I've used for years. The only difference is I substitute 1 cup of the bread crumbs with 1 cup of grated parmesan cheese in the breading. You can also add 1-2 tablespoons of parsley to the mix if you want to give it an extra nudge.
Did without the flour and breaded with saltine crackers because the store was out of bread crumbs.
Great idea for spam. I used Shake n Bake and pan fryed. It was very good. My picky kids loved it.

This is a decent recipe. I don't love spam, but I had nothing else to make for lunch, so I made this. If cut pretty thin, this actually does taste quite good. I didn't do the flour first, just dipped in a milk/egg mix, and then italian bread crumbs. Fried in a pan until brown. Thanks for a quick, simple lunch idea!
Mmmm... get these in chunks at the MN state fair as "Spam Curds". Drizzle with ranch and barbeque sauce. Yummy!

This is so good! We are trying to save money, so I am buying in bulk and going to the store a lot less. I didn't know what to do with Spam. I didn't have seasoned bread crumbs. I had cornflake crumbs, and added some italian seasoning. That's the only thing I did different. We really liked it!
Just used a mayo/sriracha slather n then crums n parmesan.
I loved this as a kid and always used it as a " Storm Meal " and forgot about it until I just saw it here and it brought back GREAT memories of how Terrific it is.

I have to admit defeat. I guess it's true sometimes you just can't go back home. I've been searching to relive my childhood dinners when my mom would fried spam. This is the second recipe I've tried, as well as just frying it
Tasted yummy at first but 1/2 way through the first patty... it did not taste yummy....
eh. Could have been a lot better. not sure how, but it could have been.

This is such a simple comfort food recipe. Ready in less than ten minutes. Everyone loves it. The egg flavor comes through and reminds me of Loco-Moco. Always a great thing! Hubby ate his with Dijon, I had mine just hot out of the fryer.
Such a quick fix! Made with rice chopped spinach and corn and my family was good to go! Thank you so much for sharing!

Im not a spam fan! I only made it bc there wasnt any meat in my house but......i made this recipe and i think i will eat spam more often than once like every 5 years! freakin amazing ..only prob i felt was i made a thicker chunk and i could taste the spam taste so i like thinner peices!
This was OK.... I didn't DISLIKE IT.... but I didn't LOVE IT.
